risks.statement: False readiness can start oversized or ambiguous work.
risks.trigger: Any codex-ready issue fails a readiness rule.
risks.response: Remove the label and repair the issue before execution.

risks.statement: A persistence or identity slice can start before its provider foundation is verified.
risks.trigger: A data-isolation or identity-dependent issue is made ready without its provider dependency complete.
risks.response: Add the dependency and execute the provider foundation first.

risks.statement: Linear release membership can drift from the delivery manifest.
risks.trigger: A live release count or issue assignment differs from the generated release plan.
risks.response: Fail the drift gate, repair the assignment, and read back all affected releases.

risks.statement: Only one human member is available for ownership and approval.
risks.trigger: A second active human workspace member becomes available.
risks.response: Until then, require CI and a separate Codex review before named Blake Rowley release or checkpoint approval; when another human joins, require a distinct human reviewer, split issue owner and reviewer, and recalibrate capacity.

risks.statement: Scheduled Linear drift enforcement depends on a repository secret.
risks.trigger: The scheduled workflow runs without LINEAR_API_KEY.
risks.response: Fail closed and configure the read-only key before treating scheduled drift as operational.

risks.statement: Default-to-R0 classification can pull later-release behavior and its dependency chain into the first release.
risks.trigger: R0 contains behavior that is not required for the defined one-buyer, one-seller defensible-evaluation journey.
risks.response: Use an explicit R0 journey allowlist and keep enhanced behavior in its owning later release unless a smaller source-bound R0 slice exists.

risks.statement: Truncated Linear list responses can make incomplete issue text look authoritative in the delivery snapshot.
risks.trigger: A listed description contains a truncation marker or omits executable fields present only in the full issue.
risks.response: Fetch the full issue before qualification and fail readiness when full text cannot be obtained.

risks.statement: External provider access can dominate calendar delivery while remaining invisible in active-work throughput.
risks.trigger: The next dependency-safe issue lacks required provider identity, credentials, or environment configuration.
risks.response: Withhold the calendar date, report external wait separately, and do not start dependent work before provider proof passes.

risks.statement: Unresolved release or dependency ownership defaults can hide a required prerequisite or falsely signal readiness.
risks.trigger: A DEC-REL-* validation trigger fires, new source or runtime evidence changes an ownership default, or affected work is proposed as codex-ready.
risks.response: Block readiness, revalidate the pinned source and runtime path, update the decision, dependency graph, and release policy, then regenerate and synchronize before execution.

risks.statement: A first production release without healthy provider predecessors and a live pre-mutation known-good canary can leave no proved rollback path.
risks.trigger: Production staging or promotion is attempted while any DEC-PROD-001 prerequisite is absent.
risks.response: Fail before provider mutation, provision or separately approve the bootstrap, and prove the live rollback anchor before customer traffic or domain promotion; historical receipts alone never authorize release.

risks.statement: A reversible planning contract can be mistaken for ratified product authority.
risks.trigger: Any linear_planning requirement is proposed as codex-ready or implemented without its named validation trigger closing.
risks.response: Fail readiness, re-read the Master Spec and UX fallback, validate or replace the planning default, update its checksum and decision, then resynchronize Linear.

risks.statement: Archiving canceled planning work before its crosswalk is complete can hide a still-required feature or failure path.
risks.trigger: A legacy issue or project is proposed for archive while its mapping is unresolved, reviewer-needed, or lacks live successor read-back.
risks.response: Withhold archive, preserve provenance, close the canonical contract and relations, obtain review, then regenerate the crosswalk and drift reports.

risks.statement: Stripe meter processing is asynchronous and provider identifier reuse outside its bounded window can turn a blind replay into a duplicate financial effect.
risks.trigger: A meter submission has an unknown outcome, a provider error event arrives, or a retry would occur after the pinned identifier-deduplication window.
risks.response: Keep one durable Sourcera delivery identity, stop blind replay, reconcile provider summaries/error events and owning source state, and require a Finance-safe receipt before terminal success or correction.

risks.statement: Conflicting role, pricing-version, seat-retention, or retention-registry source clauses can create a revenue-expanding, access-widening, or destructive false-ready implementation.
risks.trigger: F-007.B, F-132, F-529, or F-593 is proposed as codex-ready before its named source reconciliation and checksum refresh pass.
risks.response: Apply only the recorded reversible least-privilege or fail-closed default, keep readiness false, normalize the Master, regenerate ordered source bundles, and rerun authorization, financial, retention, migration, and exact Linear gates.

risks.statement: Duplicating titles, owners, releases, estimates, labels, or dependency prose inside issue descriptions lets Linear native fields and issue text drift independently.
risks.trigger: The ticket-integrity capture finds a native-field declaration, repeated native title, or dependency/relation section in a tracked issue description.
risks.response: Fail ticket integrity, keep behavior and proof detail in the description, move metadata and graph edges to native Linear fields, read back both sides, and regenerate the controlled capture.

risks.statement: The first F-007 customer pilot has no live cohort baseline, so an unversioned threshold or one-person safety result could create false release confidence.
risks.trigger: F-007.E starts collection without the approved target-set hash, treats the safety run as release proof, changes a threshold after enrollment, or has fewer than five valid starts across three consented Organizations.
risks.response: Stop the pilot, preserve the immutable failed or safety-only receipt, require independent target approval and scorecard regeneration, then run a fresh consented cohort under one frozen target version.

risks.statement: Multiple feature issues editing the central Convex schema file can silently merge incompatible tables, indexes, or generated types.
risks.trigger: A feature issue lists convex/schema.ts, uses wildcard fragment discovery, duplicates a table or index key, or generated types differ from the explicit fragment registry.
risks.response: Fail code generation and CI, keep F-005 as the sole assembler owner, return the change to its exact feature fragment, and rerun collision, generated-model, migration, and Linear path readback gates.
